picks.reasoning: Smash is the most dangerous carry on this server, and in a long series I back the star who can drag a game back from the dead, which is exactly what he did to T1. The report also flags a big region gap for the LCK, and I'm not going to ignore it. BLG have the stars to make this ugly, with Viper and Knight both able to take a lane and snowball it, but I won't hand them a 3-0 just because the room loves them after the HLE sweep. usedLessons.text: Top lesson: Individual skill still wins series, but in a Bo1 I have to check whether the star's lane can actually turn that edge into a lead before I treat it as the whole argument. When the opposing team has a proven jungle-support duo that can steal a messy game, I should rate that duo as skill too, not dismiss it as chaos, and I should be more skeptical of a Viper-sized edge when the whole BLG team is the one the crowd is backing. (from Swiss BLG vs MKOI; picked BLG, actual MKOI 1-0)

Top lesson: Individual skill still wins series, but a star's lane edge only counts if it turns into a lead that carries past the early game, so I should stop assuming three lane advantages beat one elite player like Creme who can pull games into a scramble. Next time I'll weigh whether the stronger players can actually close games when a rival star neutralizes the map. I won't let BLG's depth or the crowd's hype carry a confident 2-0. (from Swiss BLG vs TES; picked BLG 2-0, actual TES 2-1)

Top lesson: Skill won again, because DK had the better player in more lanes and Smash outplayed everyone, so one star like Caps can't outweigh a talent edge across the map. Keep judging the matchup player by player, leave region talk out unless the report flags a big gap, and ignore the "2-0 in their heads" vibes the crowd loves. (from Swiss G2 vs DK; picked DK, actual DK 1-0)

Top lesson: My core belief holds: individual skill wins series, but I should have weighted the best individual on the server, Smash, above my "more lanes" tally, because in a Bo1 one dominant player with draft priority can outweigh the other four matchups. Next time I'll check which side has the single most dangerous carry and whether the draft is likely to feed him, instead of assuming broad roster edges will override that. (from Swiss T1 vs DK; picked T1, actual DK 1-0)

When one side looks loose and together after a big win (as BLG did after beating HLE), I should treat that momentum as stronger evidence than the other side's steadiness, and not call a five-game war on the strength of one comeback story.
